title: Mini-Project #02: Identifying Environmentally Responsible US Public Transit Systems
text: As the Executive Director of the Green Transit Alliance (GTA), this project examines the environmental performance of public transportation agencies across the United States to identify those that stand out and those with room for improvement. To conduct this analysis, we combine data from the National Transit Database (NTD Service & Energy) and the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). These sources provide information on passenger trips, passenger miles, energy consumption, and estimated carbon dioxide emissions. After exploring and gathering data, our findings ultimately lead to the presentation of two awards: the Greenest Transit Agency Award and the Biggest Polluter Award.

Show Import Code
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)

load_ntd_service <- function(){
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)
  
  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
    
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
  }
  
  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()

text:
Emissions per Passenger Trip


Show Code
# Calculate emissions for each agency

AGENCY_EMISSIONS <- Final_Table|>
  group_by(NTD_ID, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarise(
    total_CO2 = sum(total_emissions),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate total passenger usage for each agency
AGENCY_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  summarise(
    total_trips = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join datasets and calculate emissions efficiency
AGENCY_EFFICIENCY <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  inner_join(
    AGENCY_SERVICE,
    by = "NTD_ID",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    CO2_per_UPT = if_else(
      total_trips > 0,
      total_CO2 / total_trips,
      NA_real_
    ),
    CO2_per_mile = if_else(
      passenger_miles > 0,
      total_CO2 / passenger_miles,
      NA_real_
    ),
    agency_size = case_when(
      total_trips < 500000 ~ "Small",
      total_trips < 5000000 ~ "Medium",
      TRUE ~ "Large"
    )
  )

# Five most efficient agencies per size category
TOP_UPT <- AGENCY_EFFICIENCY |>
  filter(!is.na(CO2_per_UPT)) |>
  group_by(agency_size) |>
  slice_min(CO2_per_UPT, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()





TOP_UPT |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    agency_size,
    total_trips,
    CO2_per_UPT
  ) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "agency_size") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Most Efficient Transit Agencies by Passenger Trip",

    total_trips = "Annual Passenger Trips (Millions)",
    CO2_per_UPT = "CO₂ (lbs/trip)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = total_trips,
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
  columns = total_trips,
  scale_by = 1/1000000,
  decimals = 2
) |>
   fmt_number(
    columns = CO2_per_UPT,
    decimals = 2
   )|>

The Greenest Transit Agency Award goes too …
The Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon has earned the Greenest Transit Agency Award, recording the lowest estimated carbon dioxide emissions per passenger mile among 219 eligible public transportation agencies. With approximately 270.79 million passenger miles annually, the Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation of Oregon generated an estimated 26.28 million pounds of CO2, equivalent to 0.097 pounds per passenger mile.
To figure out who the winner of this award, each agency’s estimated total CO2 emissions was divided by its annual passenger miles. And to be qualify for this award, Agencies were required to be U.S. only agencies, have at least 500,000 annual passenger trips and 10 million passenger miles. After gathering all the eligible agencies, the median came out to be 0.814 pounds of CO2 per passenger mile. 8. Executive Memo
To: Netflix Leadership Team
From: Jeffrey Flores
Subject: Content Strategy Recommendations for 2027 and Beyond
With increasing competition in the streaming industry, Netflix must continue to find ways to attract viewers while keeping its existing audience engaged. After examining Netflix’s viewership data from 2023 through the first half of 2026, I believe the company should focus on three areas: balancing major original releases with consistently watched content, continuing to invest in TV shows, and continue to expand into live programming.
When analyzing the top 15 titles from Netflix’s catalog, I observed that high average viewing hours didn’t necessarily mean consistent viewership. This could stem from a show having a positive word of mouth which caused it to reach such a high average view count but eventually those viewers went away, which would explain their lack of consistent viewership. Looking at the top 15 titles dataset, we saw that the Night Agent: Season 1 accumulated an average of 222.2 million viewing hours with a coefficient of variation of 119.5%. In comparison, Pablo Escobar, el patrón del mal: Season 1 averaged 136.2 million hours but had a much lower coefficient of variation of 16.8%. The Night Agent’s higher CV indicates greater fluctuations in viewership across all the periods. Pablo Escobar’s lower CV suggests steadier viewing hours. This suggests that consistent viewership can be valuable even when a title does not reach the same peaks as Netflix’s biggest hits. Netflix should continue to make and invest in productions that can maintain long-term audience engagement.
Moving onto the importance of TV shows, we saw they accounted for a much larger share of Netflix’s overall viewership. In the latest period, TV shows accounted for approximately 94.7% of total viewing hours, compared with 2.8% for movies. It’s important to note that this discrepancy can be explained by the fact that a season of a show typically has a longer runtime. Netflix should continue developing original TV series as this is where the crux of their viewership comes from. This doesn’t mean Netflix should stop producing movies, but instead put more thought into decisions on how its budget is allocated, as the data shows that a TV series provides a greater overall contribution to Netflix’s total viewing hours than movies.
Finally, live programming has shown potential to provide Netflix with a great boost in viewers. Live events averaged approximately 1.53 million views, compared with 1.37 million for prerecorded content. These live events provide Netflix with a substantial number of viewers to their streaming service in a short time. It is a great way to attract new customers to the platform in the hopes of retaining them as long-time customers. Netflix should continue to expand into live programming, particularly through events which have demonstrated strong audience interest.
To conclude, for 2027 and beyond, I believe Netflix’s content strategy should focus on maintaining long-term engagement, further expansion into live programming, and investing in TV series (whether that be original or licensed TV shows). By combining these 3 strategies, Netflix can work on maintaining a competitive edge in the industry, attract and retain a new customer base, and keep its existing customers engaged.

The Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon has earned the Greenest Transit Agency Award, recording the lowest estimated carbon dioxide emissions per passenger mile among 217 eligible public transportation agencies. With approximately 270.79 million passenger miles annually, the Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation of Oregon generated an estimated 26.28 million pounds of CO2, equivalent to 0.097 pounds per passenger mile.
To figure out who the winner of this award, each agency’s estimated total CO2 emissions was divided by its annual passenger miles. And to be qualify for this award, Agencies were required to be U.S. only agencies, have at least 500,000 annual passenger trips and 10 million passenger miles. After gathering all the eligible agencies, the median came out to be 0.814 pounds of CO2 per passenger mile.
